ISRAEL (THE NORTH): 19 RULERS JEROBOAM I → HOSHEA
“Omri slept with his fathers ... and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.” 1 Kings 16:28
“Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that were before him”
“as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat”
“There was none like unto Ahab, which did sell himself to work wickedness in the sight of the LORD, whom Jezebel his wife stirred up.” 1 Kings 21:25
When Elijah pronounced judgement after Naboth's death, Ahab tore his clothes and fasted; the LORD said “I will not bring the evil in his days: but in his son’s days”. 1 Kings 21:27–29
Chronicles: after Ramoth-gilead, Jehu son of Hanani asked Jehoshaphat, “Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the LORD?” 2 Chronicles 19:2

Each mark sits at the year of the reign the Bible gives for it.
Baal worship at court: an altar and “house of Baal” in Samaria, and a grove. 1 Kings 16:32–33
Four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and four hundred “of the groves” ate at Jezebel's table. 1 Kings 18:19
Yet seven thousand in Israel had not bowed to Baal. 1 Kings 19:18
El Elijah the Tishbite “I have found thee: because thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the LORD”
An An unnamed prophet Promised victory over the army of Ben-hadad, and warned that the king of Syria would come again.
Am A man of God Promised victory at Aphek because the Syrians said the LORD was “God of the hills”.
On One of the sons of the prophets “thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people”
Mi Micaiah son of Imlah “If thou return at all in peace, the LORD hath not spoken by me”
Ze Zedekiah son of Chenaanah Made horns of iron: “With these shalt thou push the Syrians”.

The Bible does not mention the battle of Qarqar or Ahab's part in it; that is known only from Shalmaneser's monolith.
Scripture gives no age for Ahab and does not name his mother.
Kings names “the ivory house” and “all the cities that he built” but does not say where they were.
From the textAhab son of Omri, king of Israel; not the false prophet Ahab son of Kolaiah (Jeremiah 29:21).
From the textThe site's person data links the Ben-hadad of 1 Kings 20 to the Ben-hadad of Asa's day (1 Kings 15:18); Scripture itself does not say whether they are one man. 1 Kings 20:1
